turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.

"I have until 4:40. You asked for this meeting, so let's start with what you're basing the zero on.

I'll want the basis in writing, and I'll want to know who else has seen Owen's essay."
Okay. Setting the grade aside for a second.

"Setting the grade aside for a second." Why would we do that? The grade is the reason I'm here.

My son found out about a zero from a gradebook, on his phone, in the middle of class. Nobody called me. So what is it you want to talk about first, and who decided that was the order?
If you were me, what would you do here? Genuinely.

"Genuinely." Is that a question or a way of getting me to say what I'd settle for?

Fine. If I were you, I'd have put the evidence in front of Owen before anything touched a gradebook. I'd have asked him to explain it and written down what he said. Then I'd have called his mother. A zero comes after all of that, if it comes at all.

I don't think that's what happened here. So tell me what did. Who made the decision, on what date, and was Owen heard before it was made?
